prd.title: Wedding invitation meetup scheduler (청첩장모임 스케줄러)
prd.domain: group meetup scheduling for engaged couples

scope.problem: Engaged Korean couples must hand-deliver wedding invitations through dozens of small meetups in the ~3 months before the wedding; grouping acquaintances into meetups is hard (multi-circle membership, some 1:1), and coordinating each group's date across multiplying messenger chat rooms becomes unmanageable.
scope.audience: Korean engaged couples (bride and groom using the product together, each managing their own acquaintance pool) and their 40-100+ invited acquaintances responding to date polls, with weekends filling up in the 3 months before the wedding.
jobs: Register and manage an acquaintance pool with names, relationship groups, and contacts, allowing one person in multiple groups
Compose meetups by selecting acquaintances into a group
Propose multiple candidate dates to a meetup and collect available/unavailable replies with a reply deadline
Confirm a final date and share it with all meetup members
View all confirmed meetups across both partners' pools in one calendar and spot date conflicts
Track meetup progress states: awaiting replies, ready to confirm, confirmed, completed
featureScope: feat.pool (p0): Acquaintance pool management — name, relationship group, contact; multi-group membership
feat.compose (p0): Meetup composition — bind selected acquaintances into one meetup, incl. 1:1 meetups
feat.poll (p0): Date polling and reply collection — multiple candidate dates, available/unavailable replies, reply deadline
feat.confirm (p0): Confirmation and sharing — final date visible to every meetup member
feat.overview (p0): Whole-schedule overview — all confirmed meetups across groom-side and bride-side pools, overlap detection
feat.status (p1): Progress states — awaiting replies, ready to confirm, confirmed, held

competitors.name: Doodle

rationale.sharedProblem: Coordinating one date across a group of people without endless back-and-forth in chat/email threads — the same core pain as picking a date per invitation meetup.
rationale.sharedAudience: Organizers of informal group events (friends, family, colleagues) proposing dates to invitees who reply with availability; overlaps directly with a couple polling each meetup group, though not Korea- or wedding-specific.
sharedJobs: Propose multiple candidate dates and collect availability replies (Group Poll)
Set a poll deadline for responses
Confirm a final option and notify all participants
See responses/status at a glance as votes come in
featureOverlap: feat.poll — Group Poll with multiple date/time options and yes/no/if-need-be votes, plus poll deadlines
feat.confirm — finalize the winning option and push it to participants/calendars
feat.status — organizer dashboard shows who has and hasn't responded

accessLimitations: Premium features (deadlines, reminders, ad-free) sit behind Doodle Pro, so some flows are only fully visible with a paid account
Actual poll-creation UI requires creating an account/poll; marketing pages describe but do not show every screen
No acquaintance-pool or multi-meetup overview concept — evidence limited to per-poll flows

competitors.name: Rallly

rationale.sharedProblem: Finding the best date for a group event by voting on candidate dates instead of debating in message threads — the per-meetup half of the couple's problem.
rationale.sharedAudience: Casual organizers scheduling group meetups with participants who vote via a shared link without signing up — matching acquaintances who must reply frictionlessly to a couple's poll.
sharedJobs: Propose multiple candidate dates for one gathering
Collect available/unavailable votes from participants via a shareable link
Finalize a date and notify voters
Track incoming votes and comments in real time
featureOverlap: feat.poll — date polls with per-option availability voting and comments
feat.confirm — 'finalize' step that locks the chosen date and informs participants
feat.status — live vote counts show whether a poll is still awaiting replies

accessLimitations: Pro plan gates some features (persistent polls, spaces), so free-tier screenshots may miss paid UI
Marketing site is concise; deeper feature evidence lives in the GitHub repo (https://github.com/lukevella/rallly) and docs rather than screen galleries
English-first product; no Korean-market or couple/two-organizer concepts

competitors.name: WhenSee (웬시)

rationale.sharedProblem: Korean-language 약속잡기: collecting everyone's possible dates for a 모임 through a shared voting link instead of a messy KakaoTalk room — the same chat-room-overload pain the PRD names.
rationale.sharedAudience: Korean organizers of social meetups (모임/회식) and their invitees who vote without registration — culturally and linguistically the closest match to a Korean couple's acquaintances replying to date polls.
sharedJobs: Create a poll with candidate dates (date-only voting supported)
Share a link so members reply with available times without signing up
See overlapping availability and get a recommended date
Settle the final meetup date for the group
featureOverlap: feat.poll — candidate-date voting with date-only mode and custom options (e.g. 점심/저녁 회식)
feat.confirm — recommended/decided date surfaced to all participants
feat.overview (partial) — real-time availability visualization across all respondents for one meetup

accessLimitations: Small single-product site: feature copy exists (steps + FAQ) but there is no extensive screen gallery, so screenshot evidence must come from the live app flow
Creator flow requires Google login to demonstrate end-to-end (participants need none)
Single-poll scope: no acquaintance pool, no cross-meetup calendar, no couple/dual-pool concept — absence claims need explicit page evidence

competitorRanking.rationale: Broadest evidenced coverage of the PRD (poll with deadlines, confirm with calendar push, per-poll status, a dedicated 1:1 flow, and a dashboard overview — 5 of 6 features touched), making it the primary functional benchmark despite paid gating on deadlines.

Closest market and UX fit: Korean-language, no-signup link-based replies and a heatmap overlap view directly match the PRD's casual invitee flow, and its visuals (heatmap grid, 01-04 onboarding) are the best design reference even though pool/compose/status are unevidenced.

Well-documented poll/confirm/invite-tracking flows worth borrowing (final date pinned on the shared poll page, per-invitee opened/responded indicators), but it has the most unknown cells, an explicit deadline gap, and Pro-gates its finalize step.

references.title: Visibility of System Status (Usability Heuristic #1)
references.whyRelevant: Grounds the PRD's four-state meetup lifecycle (awaiting replies / ready to confirm / confirmed / completed) and the reply-tracking patterns seen in Doodle and Rallly in the canonical status-visibility heuristic.

references.title: Date-Input Form Fields: UX Design Guidelines
references.whyRelevant: Free NN/g guidance on calendar pickers vs typed input - directly informs how organizers should propose candidate dates (near-term social events, multi-date/range selection) as Doodle, Rallly, and WhenSee all do with calendar-based option picking.

references.title: How to Use When2Meet in 2026: Step-by-Step (and When to Switch)
references.whyRelevant: Free pattern write-up of the availability-heatmap grid - the same pattern WhenSee's cards flag as the best visual benchmark - including its known gap (no explicit 'pick the winner' confirm action) that the PRD's confirm step should close.

references.title: Rallly GitHub Repository README
references.whyRelevant: Open-source repo (named in the stage source plan) whose README states the link-first, no-account voting flow, availability grid, and finalize-and-notify step in the product's own words, corroborating the Rallly cards and showing the pattern is buildable on an open Tailwind stack.

references.title: shadcn/ui Calendar Component
references.whyRelevant: Freely available design-system calendar component (same Tailwind/Radix lineage Rallly is built with) supporting single-date and range selection - a concrete default the PRD can defer unspecified visual properties to, since the client specified no brand colors or fonts.

referenceDistillation.direction: Keep the invitee path link-first and signup-free (name-only reply, as WhenSee and Rallly document) while making the organizer path stateful: every reply, the reply deadline, and the confirm action should visibly advance the meetup through the four lifecycle states, applying NN/g's status-visibility heuristic. Ship the deadline as a free core interaction that auto-locks replies at the cutoff and flips the meetup to 'ready to confirm' - Doodle paywalls this and Rallly explicitly lacks it, so it is a cheap differentiator. Confirming must be one explicit action that pins the date on the shared page, notifies every member, and closes the poll - combining Doodle's push-to-everyone guarantee with Rallly's pinned-result pattern and closing When2meet's 'no pick-the-winner button' gap; per-invitee responded indicators paired with a nudge action tell the organizer exactly whom to chase.
referenceDistillation.rationale: Stage-2 evidence shows the winning interactions are split across competitors: Doodle has deadline auto-lock and confirm-with-calendar-push but paywalls both behind Professional; Rallly has pinned finalization and per-invitee opened/responded tracking but no deadline at all ('No, this feature is currently not supported') and Pro-gates finalize; WhenSee has the frictionless no-signup reply and auto-highlighted best slots but no evidenced states or deadline. Unifying all four - free deadline, explicit confirm, no-signup replies, visible lifecycle states - is directly supported by the evidence and by NN/g's principle that communicating current state drives user control and trust.

referenceDistillation.direction: Structure the app around three surfaces: (1) a month-grid calendar picker for proposing candidate dates (NN/g: the right pattern for events within a year, and the pattern Doodle/Rallly/WhenSee all use); (2) a per-meetup shared result page that is the single canonical surface - availability heatmap with per-slot counts and auto-highlighted unanimous/majority slots on top, and the finalized date pinned on the same page once confirmed, as Rallly does; (3) a home dashboard that lists meetups grouped by the PRD's four lifecycle states and adds a cross-pool confirmed-meetups calendar merging both partners' pools with visible date-conflict flags. The merged conflict calendar is deliberately beyond any competitor's layout - Doodle's dashboard is a flat single-account list and no competitor detects overlaps.
referenceDistillation.rationale: The top-3 evidence converges on calendar-in, heatmap-out as the proven per-meetup layout (WhenSee's heatmap with counts, Rallly's calendar option picking and availability grid), and Rallly's 'final date is displayed on your poll for everyone to see' shows that pinning the outcome on the page members already visit beats a separate announcement surface. Doodle's overview card shows aggregate dashboards exist but stop at flat lists with no cross-pool view or clash detection - so the PRD's state-grouped dashboard plus merged couple calendar is where layout can differentiate rather than imitate.

referenceDistillation.direction: The client specified no colors or fonts, so all unspecified visual properties defer to the selected design system's defaults - recommended: shadcn/ui's neutral, token-driven Tailwind palette (the same open lineage Rallly ships on), which stays warm and casual rather than corporate. Reserve color for meaning: a single-hue intensity ramp (dark = most available, white = none, with a 0-to-All legend) for availability heatmaps, and one soft accent for selected candidate dates and the confirmed date, echoing WhenSee's clean heatmap benchmark and NN/g's soft-highlight range example. Keep typography and chrome minimal so the grid and calendar carry the visual weight, matching WhenSee's instantly legible 01-04 onboarding aesthetic. This direction works within the (empty) brand constraints and proposes no replacement branding.
referenceDistillation.rationale: WhenSee - the closest market/UX fit per stage 2 - is the only competitor whose cards carry positive visualPreference notes, and both point to the same taste: a clean Mon-Fri intensity heatmap with a legend and a light four-step walkthrough. The Toss-up write-up confirms the intensity-ramp encoding is the established convention for group availability, and Rallly demonstrates the neutral Tailwind look succeeds in this exact product category, so defaulting to shadcn/ui tokens borrows a proven style at zero brand risk.

ideas: A persistent, relationship-grouped acquaintance pool with multi-group membership has no evidenced counterpart in any competitor — the clearest differentiation candidate in this run.
All three competitors use per-poll link sharing or ad-hoc email entry; a pool that pre-fills invitees would remove the re-typing cost Doodle/Rallly docs imply.
Keep the pool lightweight (name + group + contact) so it stays closer to WhenSee's low-friction ethos than to a full CRM.
Doodle treats 1:1 as its own product with a simplified flow (offer times, one person picks) — model the PRD's boss-type 1:1 meetup as a streamlined variant rather than a group of one.
No competitor binds pre-registered people into a persistent meetup unit; compose-from-pool is a differentiator that pairs with feat.pool.
Retain a WhenSee-style share-link fallback so members outside the pool can still join without registration.
Reply deadlines are paid-only in Doodle, explicitly absent in Rallly, and unmentioned by WhenSee — shipping a free deadline with auto-lock (Doodle's behavior) is a concrete edge.
Doodle's 'if-need-be' middle option is worth adopting beyond binary available/unavailable replies.
WhenSee's no-signup, name-only reply flow is the friction bar to match for invitee participation.
Combine Rallly's pattern (final date pinned on the same page members voted at) with Doodle's push (calendar invite/email) so visibility does not depend on members revisiting a link.
Adopt WhenSee's auto-highlighting of unanimous vs majority slots to make the organizer's confirm decision nearly one-click.
Rallly gates finalize behind Pro — keeping confirmation free removes a competitor's monetization wall from the core loop.

Cross-meetup overlap detection is evidenced nowhere: Doodle offers only a flat dashboard list and WhenSee's heatmap is per-poll — the groom/bride whole-schedule view with clash detection is unserved territory.
Reuse WhenSee's color-intensity heatmap grammar at the cross-meetup level (confirmed dates on one calendar, clashes flagged).
Competitors delegate clash-spotting to the user's external calendar via export; doing it in-product is the PRD's chance at 'recognition rather than recall'.
Neither Doodle (open/booked/past) nor Rallly (per-invitee opened/responded) has an explicit 'ready to confirm' state — the PRD's four-state lifecycle is more expressive than anything evidenced.
Pair status with action like Doodle: surface non-responders directly in the overview next to a remind button.
Rallly's per-invitee opened/responded indicators are Pro-only; offering them free strengthens the who-to-nudge loop for informal organizers.

limitations: All five public pages describe the flow as create poll → share link → participants self-join by entering a name ('초대받은 사람은 가입 없이 이름만 입력하면 바로 참여할 수 있어요'); no page mentions picking members before sharing.
The poll-creation UI itself sits behind Google login, so an in-app member-selection step cannot be ruled out; kept 'unknown' rather than 'explicit_absence'.

cards.claim: No evidence of explicit progress states (awaiting replies / ready to confirm / confirmed / already held). The site implies at least two informal phases — collecting replies and a confirmed date — but never names lifecycle states, and the '내 일정' (My Schedules) dashboard where such states would live requires login.
limitations: Searched all five public pages for state/status language (대기, 확정됨, 완료, 진행 등); only the act of confirming ('결과를 보고 약속을 확정하세요') is described, with no state model.
The creator dashboard behind Google login is exactly where a status list would appear, so this is an access limitation rather than confirmed absence.

cards.claim: NN/g's first usability heuristic supports the PRD's explicit meetup lifecycle states and reply-tracking: communicating current system state lets users act appropriately and builds trust - the theoretical basis for surfacing awaiting-replies / ready-to-confirm / confirmed / completed states and non-responder indicators (as Doodle and Rallly partially do).

decisionRationales: feat.pool and cross-meetup feat.overview are the strongest differentiators: no competitor evidences a relationship-grouped acquaintance pool, and overlap detection across confirmed meetups appears nowhere — Doodle's dashboard is a flat list and WhenSee's heatmap is single-poll only.

Reply deadlines are a competitive gap in the poll core: Doodle gates them behind a paid plan and Rallly's FAQ states outright they are unsupported, so a free deadline with auto-lock is a low-cost edge.

Every 'unknown' cell in this run is an access limitation (logged-in dashboards at Doodle, Rallly, and WhenSee were not inspected), not confirmed absence — only Rallly's deadline gap met the explicit_absence bar; treat unknowns as risks to re-verify, not settled gaps.

For confirmation visibility, the evidence supports combining two proven patterns: pin the final date at the link members already use (Rallly) and push it to calendars/inboxes (Doodle), so no member depends on revisiting the poll.

WhenSee is the closest UX reference for the target audience: no-signup name-only participation and the availability heatmap directly match the PRD's casual Korean invitees, even though its feature breadth is narrowest.
